subject: biology

moments.title: C. elegans connectome
moments.body: After decades of reconstruction from electron micrographs, Brenner's group publishes the wiring diagram of the entire C. elegans nervous system — 302 neurons, ~7,000 connections.
moments.takeaway: The first complete connectome — a 302-neuron worm.

moments.title: Human Connectome Project
moments.body: Multi-institutional project maps human white-matter pathways with diffusion MRI. The macroscopic human connectome is published.
moments.takeaway: The human brain's wiring is mapped at the millimetre scale.

moments.title: Fly brain hemisphere
moments.body: Electron microscopy reconstructs ~25,000 neurons and ~20 million synapses in half the fruit-fly brain.
moments.takeaway: A whole insect brain mapped at synapse resolution.

moments.title: Cubic millimetre of human cortex
moments.body: A 1 mm^3 piece of human cerebral cortex is reconstructed at synaptic resolution: ~57,000 cells, 150 million synapses, 1.4 petabytes of data.
moments.takeaway: Slowly, the human brain is being reconstructed neuron by neuron.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Connectomics increasingly uses ML for image reconstruction. Goal: full mouse brain connectome (~70 million neurons). Eventually, the human cortex.
now.open_questions: How much does the connectome reveal about function? Will it explain consciousness?

reflection: C. elegans took decades for 302 neurons. Human brain has 86 billion. When does scale outrun any feasible approach?
